// Must-trip fixture (TestStrykerPrePhaseBranchTrips): the stryker.go branch
// tool-output-not-persisted removed, from 6f27eaa^, with minimal stubs. The
// tee, headBuffer, quote(), the reportless errors.New(msg) and
// checkInstrumented's Errorf are copied verbatim (lines 115-118, 142, 150,
// 176-222 and 315 of that file; TestStrykerPrePhaseBranchIsPinned holds them
// byte for byte), plus the spec's two-line paraphrase: the head rendered into
// a strings.Builder, quoted.String() passed to fmt.Errorf on the next line.
package stryker

import (
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
)

const (
	strykerHeadBytes = 64 << 10
	strykerHeadLines = 40

	strykerInitialTestFailureText    = "One or more tests failed in the initial test run"
	strykerInitialTestTruncationNote = "the list above may be truncated"
	strykerDropWarningText           = "did not result in any files"
)


// headBuffer retains the first `limit` bytes written through it and silently
// discards the rest, always reporting a full write so it can sit inside an
// io.MultiWriter without truncating the stream its sibling is rendering.
type headBuffer struct {
	limit int
	buf   bytes.Buffer
}

func (h *headBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if room := h.limit - h.buf.Len(); room > 0 {
		if len(p) <= room {
			h.buf.Write(p)
		} else {
			h.buf.Write(p[:room])
		}
	}
	// len(p), never the amount kept: a short count is an io.ErrShortWrite to
	// io.MultiWriter, which would abort the write to os.Stderr as well and
	// truncate the live output the moment the cap was reached.
	return len(p), nil
}

func (h *headBuffer) quote(n int) string {
	text := strings.TrimRight(h.buf.String(), "\n")
	if text == "" {
		return "stryker produced no output at all — it may not have started."
	}
	lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
	truncated := false
	if len(lines) > n {
		lines, truncated = lines[:n], true
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("the head of stryker's output, which is where the cause is:\n\n")
	for _, l := range lines {
		b.WriteString("    ")
		b.WriteString(l)
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	if truncated {
		b.WriteString("    … (output continues above)\n")
	}
	return b.String()
}

// run is the branch around the tee, cut to what the escape needs.
func run(cmd *exec.Cmd, reportPath string) ([]byte, error) {
	head := &headBuffer{limit: strykerHeadBytes}
	sink := io.MultiWriter(os.Stderr, head)
	cmd.Stdout = sink
	cmd.Stderr = sink
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
		if !errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
			printHead(os.Stderr, head)
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("stryker invocation failed: %w", err)
		}
	}

	b, err := os.ReadFile(reportPath)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			msg := fmt.Sprintf("stryker did not write a report at %s.\n%s", reportPath, head.quote(strykerHeadLines))
			if strings.Contains(head.buf.String(), strykerInitialTestFailureText) {
				msg += "\n" + strykerInitialTestTruncationNote
			}
			return nil, errors.New(msg) // WANT taint
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read stryker report: %w", err)
	}
	if err := checkInstrumented(nil, head); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return b, nil
}

// checkInstrumented, cut to its escape.
func checkInstrumented(dropped []string, head *headBuffer) error {
	if len(dropped) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	msg := fmt.Sprintf("stryker instrumented none of %d file(s) it was asked to mutate: %s.\n",
		len(dropped), strings.Join(dropped, ", "))
	if strings.Contains(head.buf.String(), strykerDropWarningText) {
		msg += "stryker said so itself — look for \"" + strykerDropWarningText + "\" below.\n"
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("%s\n%s", msg, head.quote(strykerHeadLines)) // WANT taint
}

// paraphrase is the spec's c-3 shape in two lines.
func paraphrase(head *headBuffer) error {
	var quoted strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprint(&quoted, head.quote(strykerHeadLines))
	return fmt.Errorf("stryker failed:\n%s", quoted.String()) // WANT taint
}

// printHead is where the head belongs: the terminal.
func printHead(w io.Writer, h *headBuffer) { fmt.Fprint(w, h.quote(strykerHeadLines)) }

var _ = bytes.MinRead
